promptLatex: In a group of 60 students, 35 take math, 30 take physics, and 20 take chemistry. 12 take both math and physics, 8 take both math and chemistry, and 5 take both physics and chemistry. 3 take all three subjects. How many students take exactly one subject?
hintLatex: First compute the number who take at least one subject using inclusion-exclusion.
Then subtract those who take exactly two and exactly three subjects.
Or compute directly: (only math) + (only physics) + (only chemistry).
Only math: 35 - 12 - 8 + 3 = 18 (subtract those in intersections, add back the triple).
solutionLatex: Using inclusion-exclusion, compute the number of students in each exclusive region.
